query: Consider the following context: Noble metal–based high-entropy alloys (NM-HEAs) are promising catalysts because of their diverse compositions and complex surface structures, although understanding their formation and achieving precise atomic control remain challenging. In that context, which method can be used for produce HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Electrodeposition can be used to produce HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
generation.material_initial_state: Noble metal ions in a solution
generation.mechanism: Reduction of metal ions on the electrode surface
generation.boundary: Limited by the electrode material and solution composition
generation.uncertainty: The exact conditions and parameters for electrodeposition to produce HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks are unknown due to insufficient evidence.

falsification_experiment.design: Comparative study of electrodeposition and other methods for producing HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If electrodeposition does not produce HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks with desired structure and catalytic activity, the hypothesis is falsified.
